questions.topic: Day 2 · Segment 3: Laser Shaft Alignment Analysis
questions.prompt: Why should alignment tolerances match the machine and coupling?
questions.answer: Acceptable misalignment depends on the application specification
options: Acceptable misalignment depends on the application specification
Every coupling has the same tolerance
The loosest displayed setting is always correct
questions.explanation: Use the coupling specification and shaft speed as directed rather than an arbitrary acceptable screen result.
questions.section: C302 Laser Shaft Alignment.pdf, PDF page 17

reviewCue.text: Review C302 Laser Shaft Alignment.pdf, PDF page 17. Use the coupling specification and shaft speed as directed rather than an arbitrary acceptable screen result.

questions.topic: Day 2 · Segment 3: Laser Shaft Alignment Analysis
questions.prompt: How does the described backlash check compare readings?
questions.answer: Rotate one direction, then reverse and compare
options: Rotate one direction, then reverse and compare
Add equal shims to every foot
questions.explanation: Reversing rotation reveals mechanical play that can distort angular readings.

reviewCue.text: Review C302 Laser Shaft Alignment.pdf, slide 41. Reversing rotation reveals mechanical play that can distort angular readings.

questions.topic: Day 2 · Segment 3: Laser Shaft Alignment Analysis
questions.prompt: A sensor shifts but the screen still appears in tolerance. What is required?
questions.answer: Secure it and recalibrate or remeasure as prompted
options: Secure it and recalibrate or remeasure as prompted
Use a wider tolerance to hide the change
questions.explanation: Sensor movement can invalidate calibration even if the visible laser position looks acceptable.
